items.stem: Which particle most typically marks the direct object of a transitive verb in Japanese?

options.rationale: Correct: the particle wo marks the direct object of a transitive verb.
ga typically marks the grammatical subject, not the object.
ni marks destination, time or indirect object, not the direct object here.
e marks direction toward, not the direct object.

items.explanation: Correct: the particle wo marks the direct object of a transitive verb.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about standard Japanese sentence structure are correct?

options.text: The basic word order is subject-object-verb
The main verb usually comes at the end of the clause
options.rationale: Correct: the predicate verb is clause-final.

options.text: Modifying adjectives follow the noun they modify
options.rationale: Japanese attributive modifiers precede the noun.

options.text: Grammatical particles come before the word they mark
options.rationale: Particles follow the word they mark, not precede it.

options.text: A definite article is required before every noun

items.explanation: Correct keys: A, B. Correct: Japanese is typically SOV. Correct: the predicate verb is clause-final.
